item.title: US Retail Sales Growth Slows as Big-Ticket Purchases Slip
item.description: US retail sales growth moderated in October as a pullback in big ticket items, like cars, masked resilient demand for other goods.
item.dc:creator: Julia Fanzeres

item.title: Africa Nations to End Year With High Rates as Fed Risks Loom
item.description: African central banks from South Africa to Egypt are set to end 2026 with restrictive monetary policy, as their currencies face pressure amid expectations that the Federal Reserve will extend its interest-rate hiking cycle.
item.dc:creator: Monique Vanek

item.title: Waller Says Fed Open to ‘Responsible Innovation’ in Payments
item.description: Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller said Tuesday the central bank supports “responsible innovation” in the payments system and will continue to engage industry while providing core payment and settlement infrastructure.
item.dc:creator: Katanga Johnson

item.title: Thailand Opens Market Wider to US Goods to Secure Trade Deal
item.description: Thailand and the US nearly concluded months of trade negotiations after Bangkok made concessions to preserve access to its biggest export market, which buys about a quarter of the country’s overseas shipments.
item.dc:creator: Erich Parpart, Suttinee Yuvejwattana and Annmarie Hordern

item.title: Angola Defies Global Trend, Cuts Rates Again to 10-Year Low
item.description: Angola’s central bank remained a global outlier, cutting its key interest rate again to the lowest in more than a decade as it sees inflation continuing to slow.
item.dc:creator: Candido Mendes

item.title: Germany Corrects October Inflation Data, Showing Stronger Pace
item.description: Germany’s statistics office corrected its inflation data for October, saying the number came in stronger than initially reported.
item.dc:creator: Zoe Schneeweiss and Alexander Weber

item.title: Italy May Exit EU Monitoring Regime Next Year, Dombrovskis Says
item.description: Italy’s deficit next year will likely be below the European Union’s 3% ceiling, allowing the country to exit the bloc’s special monitoring regime, Economy Commissioner Valdis Dombrovskis said.
item.dc:creator: Jorge Valero and Alessandra Migliaccio

item.title: Chile Central Bank Says New Rules Eased Fallout From Swap Losses
item.description: Chile’s central bank said ample liquidity and new risk-based rules limiting the use of derivatives helped contain the fallout from losses on massive swap positions held by the country’s pension funds.
item.dc:creator: Carolina Gonzalez

item.title: Fed’s Musalem Says ‘Several’ Rate Hikes Likely Needed by Spring
item.description: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis President Alberto Musalem signaled support Tuesday for multiple interest rate-increases in the coming months to bring inflation under control.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Ackerman

item.title: EU and anti-dumping duties on steel and Chinese imports
item.description: Five economies including India, Taiwan and Turkey were targeted
item.dc:creator: Laura Curtis

item.title: China Hawks Ascend in Washington to Push New Tech Restrictions
item.description: Export controls on Nvidia will pose a test to the trade truce between the world’s two biggest economies.
item.dc:creator: Chris Anstey

item.title: German Investor Outlook Jumps to Highest Since Iran War Began
item.description: Germany’s investor outlook jumped to its highest level since February, as the economy looks set to grow the most in four years.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Weber

item.title: De Cos Set for Top ECB Job as Germany Picks Chief Economist
item.description: Pablo Hernandez de Cos is firmly on track to win the European Central Bank presidency after a pivotal political deal in Berlin.
item.dc:creator: Mark Schroers, Michael Nienaber and Arne Delfs

item.title: Euro Zone to Grow Robustly as It Shrugs Off Inflation, EU Says
item.description: The euro-area economy will grow robustly in the coming years, displaying further resilience to inflation that’s proving much more stubborn than policymakers expected as the Iran war broke out, according to the European Commission.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Weber

item.title: France to Miss Deficit Goals as Economic Growth Falters, EU Says
item.description: France will miss its deficit reduction goals both this year and next as the economy sputters and debt servicing costs rise, the European Commission said in another warning on the public finances of the euro area’s second largest economy.
item.dc:creator: William Horobin

item.title: Germany to Propose Markus Brunnermeier as ECB Chief Economist
item.description: Germany will propose Markus Brunnermeier as chief economist of the European Central Bank, according to people familiar with the matter
item.dc:creator: Michael Nienaber, Kamil Kowalcze and Mark Schroers

item.title: UK Payrolls Fell Unexpectedly Ahead of Healey’s Budget
item.description: UK employers cut payrolls in the run-up to the Labour government’s budget, yet economists said the jobs market remains robust enough to keep another interest rate hike in play at the Bank of England’s December meeting.
item.dc:creator: Irina Anghel

item.title: Malaysia Inks Deal With France to Develop Critical Minerals
item.description: Malaysia will cooperate with France to further develop its critical minerals industry, marking its first such tie-up with a European nation.
item.dc:creator: Danial Azhar and Kok Leong Chan

item.title: China and Canada Expand Tariff Relief as Xi Meets Carney
item.description: China and Canada agreed to further tariff relief on agriculture and steel exports as President Xi Jinping and Prime Minister Mark Carney met in Shenzhen on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Brian Platt

item.title: Japan Said to Delay Floating-Rate Bond Launch Given Weak Demand
item.description: Japan will likely delay the launch of its new floating-rate government bonds as demand wanes for hedging against rising borrowing costs, with investors expecting only a few more interest-rate hikes to remain in the current cycle.
item.dc:creator: Takashi Umekawa
